paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, Lily sat at the big library table with her laptop. She was writing an article for the class blog. The title was "A Review of the Old Town Guidebook." Her article was long, and it had many nice words about the cover and the colors. A big blue guidebook lay closed next to the laptop. The library was quiet, and only the clock on the wall made a sound. Leo came and sat beside her.

"Is that the new guidebook?" asked Leo. "Yes," said Lily. "It is very useful, and the cover is beautiful." "My review is almost ready." "Great," said Leo. "Is there a test on it?" "No," said Lily with a laugh. "It is only for the blog."

Teacher Kim stopped at their table. "Lily, may I read your article?" she asked. "Of course," said Lily. Teacher Kim read the first lines and smiled. "Nice words," she said. "Now I have two small questions." "Which page has the map of the old well?" "It is probably in the middle," said Lily.

"And which photo do you like best?" asked Teacher Kim. "The photo on the first page," said Lily. "It has a big red gate and a white bird." "And the last page has a nice picture of the river." "I see," said Teacher Kim. Teacher Kim looked at the closed guidebook and then at Lily. She did not ask a third question. Lily looked at the laptop, and her ears became pink.

"Leo, do you want to try the guidebook?" asked Teacher Kim. "Yes, please," said Leo. Leo turned the pages carefully, because the paper was thin. He opened the book in the middle and found the map in five seconds. "It is on page twenty," he said. "There is a small line of text under it too." "The well was built a long time ago." "Thank you, Leo," said Teacher Kim.

Lily held the guidebook close and thought for a moment. "Anyway," said Lily quietly, "I think I need to read the book first." "Good idea," said Teacher Kim, and she smiled. "A review is more useful when the writer knows the whole book." "Take it home tonight." "Tomorrow, you can finish your article." Lily put the guidebook in her bag and closed her laptop.
